preamble: The close-mid front unrounded vowel [e] becomes back rounded [o], usually by assimilation to a neighbouring sound with back or labial articulation. Latin backed e to o before w and before velar l (novus, holus < helus); Old Provençal did it before labials (premier > promier); and Russian turned stressed e into o after soft consonants before a hard one (о чём, ёлка).

examples.note: Stressed *e after a soft consonant became o (spelled ё) when no soft consonant followed; hence alternations like ель/ёлка, лечь/лёг.
e became o before velar l.
e became o before a labial, especially m.
